headline: Nvidia leadership shakeup overshadows a fragile post-selloff rebound
body: The dominant story in markets right now isn't a data print but a boardroom one: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned effective immediately on November 12, following board scrutiny of extramarital relationships, one of which reportedly drew scrutiny over a possible foreign-intelligence angle. CFO Colette Kress has stepped in as interim CEO while the board, now chaired for the first time by an independent director, says its investigation into the matter is continuing even as it searches for a permanent successor. The stock had already shed several percent in the days after the inquiry became public, on fears that losing its founder-CEO could unsettle the broader AI trade more than any single earnings miss. With no succession plan yet named, that open-endedness, rather than resolution, is what the market is currently pricing.

This leadership shock lands on top of an already shaky AI-stock recovery: a broad early-November selloff tied to post-election worries over tighter data-center and AI regulation knocked the Nasdaq and S&P 500 into some of their worst sessions in months, before chip stocks clawed back a meaningful chunk of the damage over the following week. The Fed is adding to the cautious tone, having held rates at its October meeting with only modest odds priced for a December cut, so there's little monetary tailwind to lean on. Nvidia's November 17 earnings, now the first under interim leadership, have turned into a bigger test of confidence than a routine print would be. Retail-sentiment chatter on the leadership change was present but not dominant in today's search results, so this read leans more on price action and governance headlines than on a clear social-media mood signal.
